description: Deterministic coding-agent eval tasks (schema 3). Each task ships its own tiny repository, a scripted model transcript and a post-run verification. No network, no Docker, no live model and no process spawn: every command a task names is a SIMULATOR inside tests/coding-agent-c6-eval.test.ts, so the corpus runs identically in CI and in a sandbox with no toolchain at all. The simulators are named for what they are. `npm test` is a REGEX SIMULATOR: it evaluates only `expect(<fn>(a, b)).toBe(n)` against `export function f(a, b) { return a <op> b; }` in JavaScript/TypeScript-shaped files and honours .skip/.todo/.only. It has NO understanding of Python, Go or any other language, and the corpus never asks it to run one: the Python and Go tasks carry no command at all and are verified by `file_contains`/`diff_stats` over the change set, which is a statement about the fixture text, never about execution. `npm run build` parses the project JSON configuration with the real JSON.parse (a build that cannot read its own configuration fails). `npm run deps:check` scans import/require specifiers and the manifest and reports undeclared imports and declared-but-unused dependencies, the two directions of a dependency migration. Neither resolves a package and no simulator spawns anything. Schema 1 tasks are the eight C6 tasks (file_contains/command_succeeds over tool and message steps); schema 2 added the C9 step kind 'check' and the change-set verifications 'test_integrity', 'self_review' (over a RECORDED provider answer), 'repair_loop' and 'command_fails'; schema 3 (C14) adds the 'diff_stats' verification plus the per-task 'taskType'/'language' coverage metadata and the turns/diffStats/costUsd scores the harness derives for every task. Every addition is additive: an older task stays valid verbatim.
